articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia strikes Kyiv hours before truce begins in war-ravaged city Oleshky
articles.body:
- Russian strikes on Kyiv killed one person and wounded eight, with mayor Vitali Klitschko saying medical facilities and an intensive care unit had been damaged in the late Monday attack. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a ballistic missile attack had struck the grounds of a university campus in the Ukrainian capital. “The missiles hit very crowded areas, and there is not a single military facility nearby. This was a strike directly on the city, on its infrastructure,” he said on social media.
- The strikes on Kyiv came hours before a truce in the ravaged Russian-occupied city of Oleshky was due to start, after months of reports that residents faced dire food, water and medicine shortages. The truce, aimed at allowing humanitarian aid into Oleshky, was to begin at 3am local time (0100 GMT). No end date for the truce has been provided. The city in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region has been caught in the crosshairs of fighting between the two sides since 2022, when it was seized by Russian forces. Neither Russia, Ukraine nor the US has said who would monitor the truce, or given details about the humanitarian operation set to accompany it. The Russian defence ministry said on Friday it would halt fire in the “Kherson sector” for the duration of the ceasefire. Ukraine has accused Russia of blocking residents from leaving, a charge Moscow has denied.
- Before the latest strikes on Kyiv, Zelenskyy highlighted Ukraine was still waiting for US defence secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on critical missile supplies. “We have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again,” he said on X.
- Romania said on Monday that a network “coordinated” from Russia was involved in starting a fire near an arms factory. The fire broke out on 14 September near an arms factory in the central city of Brasov and two Belarusians and a Ukrainian – residents in EU countries – were involved, authorities said. Two of them were “tracked down and remanded in custody in Germany while they were preparing to commit similar offences”, the office for organised crime said. The third is at large in Poland, it added. Russia’s embassy in Bucharest could not immediately be reached for comment but Moscow has repeatedly denied such accusations.
- The attack in Brasov is the latest in a string of similar incidents in Europe, with Nato and the EU grappling with what they say is a “hybrid” campaign of sabotage and interference by the Kremlin aimed at undercutting Western support for Kyiv. Over the past three weeks, at least eight cargo ships have been hit off the coast of Nato members Romania and Bulgaria. Some 34 sailors are reported dead or missing.
- Ukraine’s military has begun using specialised aerial rescue drones to evacuate wounded soldiers from the battlefield, carrying two stranded troops to safety near the Russian border in the first such operations. The newly developed StarGate drone, a six-rotor aircraft fitted with an enclosed evacuation capsule, was used in two separate missions over the past week, the 475th Separate Assault Regiment, an elite unit, said on Monday. Developed by Ukrainian technology company SkyFall, the drone is intended to reduce rescue times from hours to minutes, reaching hard-to-access combat zones currently served by unmanned ground vehicles.

Australia to host USS Colorado as first US nuclear submarine under Aukus pact
The Aukus pact, seen as a response to China’s military build-up, aims to equip Australia’s navy with a fleet of nuclear stealth submarines

The Pentagon has assigned the USS Colorado as the first US nuclear-powered attack submarine to join a rotating force to be based in Western Australia.
The 115-metre (380-foot) Virginia-class submarine, armed with land-attack missiles and sophisticated torpedoes, would sail to the new Australian base in late 2027, officials said on Tuesday.
The deployment was a “significant milestone” in building up a joint US-Australia-UK deterrence in the Pacific under their Aukus defence pact, the allies said in a joint statement.

articles.title: Russian forces introduce ceasefire in Kherson direction
articles.body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The Russian Armed Forces introduced a ceasefire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) to prepare for a humanitarian operation near Alyoshki, the Defense Ministry said in a statement.
"As part of preparations for a humanitarian operation near the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, the Russian Armed Forces ceased fire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27," the statement reads.
Russian Chief of the General Staff Army General Valery Gerasimov announced on October 23 that the Russian Armed Forces would cease fire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27 to allow for a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki.
According to the Russian Defense Ministry, the Kiev regime has been shelling roads leading to Alyoshki and extensively using drones to destroy vehicles. Ukrainian forces have also been using unmanned aerial vehicles to lay mines along roads to prevent civilian evacuations and impede the delivery of foods, medicine and other essential supplies to Alyoshki.
Over the past week alone, the Kiev regime carried out 18 artillery strikes and more than 120 drone strikes on Alyoshki and main roads in the area, while Russian troops devised over 300 landmines and other explosive devices.
On September 21, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the situation in Alyoshki as critical, saying that food and medicine could not be delivered there amid ongoing Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks. Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9. Putin said the parties had agreed that Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova would remain in constant contact with US First Lady Melania Trump's office.
Peskov pointed out on October 26 that the agreement to conduct a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki could set a precedent for similar missions in other areas. He particularly highlighted the United States’ direct and constructive role in coordinating the process. Peskov added that Russia hoped Ukraine would honor all agreements concerning the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki.

articles.title: Russia announces ceasefire in frontline town
articles.body:
Ceasefire takes effect in frontline town – Russia
A temporary ceasefire around the frontline town of Alyoshki in Russia’s Kherson Region has taken effect to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians, the Russian Defense Ministry has announced.
According to a brief statement by the ministry, the ceasefire began at 4am Moscow time (01:00 GMT) on Tuesday “in preparation for a humanitarian operation.”
General Valery Gerasimov, Russia’s chief of the General Staff, said last week that military engineers would conduct reconnaissance and ensure “the safe passage of a humanitarian convoy” into the town. The Ukrainian General Staff also confirmed last week that it would observe the truce.
Russian authorities estimate that between 1,500 and 2,000 civilians remain trapped in Alyoshki, on the left bank of the Dnieper River opposite the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson. The town has been largely cut off from supplies for months, with Ukrainian shelling and drone strikes preventing regular aid deliveries, according to Russian officials.
Ukraine has accused Russia of preventing civilians from leaving the embattled town. However, residents who managed to escape told RT earlier this month that Alyoshki was effectively under siege by Ukrainian forces, which they said were carrying out constant attacks.

articles.title: Teen arrested in Florida shooting will be tried as adult, US officials say
articles.body:
Teen arrested in Florida shooting will be tried as adult, US officials say
Billy Witz
- A 15-year-old, Anthony Rivers III, will be tried as an adult after an Oct 24 Tallahassee shooting left 11 people shot and six in hospital, one critically ill.
- Police said the gunfire followed a fight between people who knew each other, and none of the victims seemed to be intended targets. More arrests may follow.
- Prosecutor Jack Campbell said the case is severe, with 11 attempted second-degree murder charges and one firearm charge. He also linked the decision to Rivers’ past arrests.
AI generated
Tallahassee, Florida - A 15-year-old boy who was arrested in the shooting of 11 people after a college football game in Tallahassee, Florida, will stand trial as an adult, a Florida prosecutor said on Oct 26.
The teenager, Anthony Rivers III, was ordered to remain in custody at a juvenile court hearing on Oct 26 after his arrest the day before. The shooting took place in a crowded, closed-off street on Oct 24 about an hour after Florida A&M University’s homecoming game. A crowd of just over 20,000 attended the event.
The shooting left six people hospitalised as of Oct 25, one of whom was in critical condition. A spokesperson for the Leon County School District said four of its students were wounded, including the one in critical condition.
Six of the 11 people shot were minors, the Tallahassee Police Department said. A 12th person was injured but not shot, officials said.
Lawrence Revell, chief of the Tallahassee police, said at a news conference on Oct 26 that the shooting appeared to have stemmed from a physical altercation between people who knew one another and that none of the victims appeared to be intended targets. He said more arrests were possible.
Judge Andrew Sheeran, who presided over the hearing on Oct 26, said he would grant the request of the top prosecutor in Tallahassee to try Rivers as an adult, which Florida law allows in certain cases. He will be charged with 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder and one count of possession of a firearm by a delinquent, officials said.
“It’s our discretion because of the severity of the offence,” said the prosecutor, Jack Campbell.
In a phone interview, he added that he had discussed the decision with juvenile-case prosecutors before asking his prosecutors to review the case. “Ultimately, it was my decision,” he said.
Rivers, dressed in a white T-shirt, grey gym shorts, sandals and his hair pulled up into a bun, stood quietly at the hearing on Oct 26 with his hands clasped behind his back, as the public defender who is representing him addressed the court.
The public defender said she had previously represented Rivers. Her office did not reply to a request for comment. Efforts to reach relatives of Rivers were not immediately successful.
According to court records, Rivers has been arrested previously on charges including burglary and theft of a gun, but it was unclear what the outcome was. He was arrested on Sept 6 for violating his probation and had been sentenced to a juvenile home.
According to a police affidavit, Rivers was arrested after surveillance cameras and an ankle monitor he was wearing identified him at a Tallahassee mall where gunfire had erupted in an underground parking lot.
The police identified another 15-year-old who was with Rivers as the shooter, according to the affidavit. Nobody was injured in the shooting, which occurred after an altercation in the mall.
Campbell declined to discuss anything about Rivers’ criminal record. But he said if someone was a repeat offender, “that’s something we consider” when determining whether to charge a juvenile as an adult.
The shooting echoed others in Tallahassee in recent years. Nine people were shot – one fatally – outside a liquor store in 2022 that Campbell said was connected to a homecoming event at Florida A&M.
In 2025, two people were killed and six others were wounded in a shooting at Florida State University, which is adjacent to Florida A&M.
Campbell is seeking the death penalty against the shooter in that case, Phoenix Ikner, who has pleaded not guilty and is awaiting trial.
The shooting on Oct 24 could have been much worse, Campbell said.
It happened on Perry Street, a residential street that runs alongside Bragg Memorial Stadium, where the football team plays. The street was blocked off for vendors selling food and T-shirts, and it is a popular place to tailgate before and after games.
“If you go to FAMU, you’ve spent time on Perry Street,” Campbell said. NYTIMES
- Kirsten Noyes contributed research.
- This article originally appeared in The New York Times.

articles.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or, ending England’s 25-year wait
articles.body:
Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or, ending England’s 25-year wait
NewsFeed
Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or, ending England’s 25-year wait
Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has won his first Ballon d’Or after a record-breaking season, becoming the first Englishman to claim football’s top individual honour since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane scored 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season.
